› hey so i want you to take a moment and go top to bottom on the gpu/3d.zig and adjacent
  **GOD** files (you know, the ones where its like over 5k lines of code) and lets gather

• I’m treating this as engine/game-surface analysis. I’ll first register the work and
  consult the repository oracle, then inventory gpu/3d.zig and every adjacent 5k-plus-line
  “god file” top to bottom. The deliverable will be a capability map with concrete action
  groupings and code locations—no edits or speculative refactor implementation.

• The oracle has one directly relevant architectural ruling and two implementation
  hazards. The ruling separates semantic world authoring (pieces, prefabs, markers) from
  mesh/runtime rendering concerns; the hazards confirm that gpu/3d.zig also owns hot-
  reload cache cleanup and transparent-pass behavior. I’m now locating the actual
  oversized cluster and will distinguish current capability from historical/adjacent
  coupling.

• The oversized active-source set is small but cross-layer: 3d.zig (16,083), editor
  AppFrame.tsx (7,262), engine.zig (6,147), and editor ModelView.tsx (5,178). The 162k-
  line icon_atlas.zig is generated payload, not a behavioral god file. I’m treating the
  four real source files as the main inventory, then mapping the just-below-cutoff bridge/
  editor helpers where they explain ownership seams.

• The boundary is now clear: gpu/3d.zig is not one renderer with a few helpers. Roughly
  70% of it is the resident model-authoring backend (topology, semantics, undo, UV, paint,
  overlays); the remaining portion is the actual Scene3D GPU pipeline. World placement
  itself lives higher up in AppFrame and the application-command/world modules—3d.zig only
  consumes the resulting geometry and instance data. I’m doing the final cross-file
  ownership pass now, including the action vocabularies that already name the natural
  groups.

• The plain answer: framework/gpu/3d.zig:1 is currently three large systems sharing one
  stateful module:

  1. A Scene3D renderer.
  2. A host-resident model-authoring backend.
  3. The native interaction and visual-overlay backend for that editor.

  Despite the filename, roughly 70% of it is model editing, UV, paint, journal, and editor
  presentation—not GPU rendering.

  World placement is not authored there. The editor/world command layer creates and edits
  semantic pieces; 3d.zig receives the resulting mesh and instance rows and draws them.

  ## gpu/3d.zig, top to bottom

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:1, it defines the GPU-facing wire formats:

  - Packed mesh vertices.
  - Standard and foliage instance formats.
  - Scene, lighting, shadow, sky, and skinning uniforms.
  - Render-memory accounting.
  - Retained geometry cache.
  - Host-loaded GLB/OBJ stash.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:439, it becomes an editor backend:

  - Native orbit camera, framing, zoom, pan, focus, lock, and bookmarks.
  - Exact last-rendered camera/viewport capture for picking.
  - Resident edit-document identity, topology generation, stable geometry handle.
  - Indexed edit-mesh mirror and safety snapshots.
  - Loading, replacing, quality-previewing, and stashing the active model.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:941, it owns core topology transactions:

  - Mesh replacement with UV, atlas, color, group, part, material, and semantic carry.
  - Face/region extrusion.
  - Edge extrusion.
  - Face creation from edges.
  - Loop cut and connect vertices.
  - Symmetry analysis and symmetrize.
  - Captured preview sessions for loop cut and bevel.
  - Delete, weld, retopology weld-pairs, and width normalization.
  - Metadata guards that verify resident state survived each operation.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:4403, it owns document and part operations:

  - Append primitive groups.
  - Append camera-projected path planes and naked edge paths.
  - Hide/show parts while preserving their geometry and paint.
  - Compose model and painted document snapshots.
  - Track surviving group ranges.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:4988, it owns the native document journal:

  - Full geometry, UV, atlas, paint-program, part, hidden-group, and retopology snapshots.
  - Integrity roll calls.
  - Undo/redo stacks.
  - Journal notes carrying cart-side part metadata.
  - Native action-event emission.
  - Session and history JSON diagnostics.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:6063, it adds higher-level modeling operations:

  - Duplicate and mirror part ranges.
  - Path Array over curves or explicit paths.
  - Detach faces into a part.
  - Merge parts.
  - Flip winding and normalize soup winding.
  - Merge selected faces.
  - Whole-topology triangle-to-quad preview/commit.
  - Glass partitioning.
  - Solidify.
  - Gizmo safety guard and concavity repair.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:7769, it owns retopology teaching state and tool state:

  - Retopology band plans.
  - Manual band assignments.
  - Frozen source ghost.
  - Persistence and restoration of the retopology guide.
  - Active selection mode, x-ray, symmetry planes, gizmo tool, paint-session gate.
  - Picking, marquee, scope switching, and out-of-scope part detection.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:8266, it is an editor overlay renderer:

  - Move/scale/rotate gizmos and hit testing.
  - Backdrop-position gizmo.
  - Vertex snapping and numeric transform doors.
  - Modeling floor grid.
  - World axes, scale ruler, and mannequin.
  - Vertex, edge, face, glass, semantic, UV, and retopology overlays.
  - Loop-cut handles.
  - Orientation compass and camera snaps.
  - Marquee and selection presentation.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:9786, it exposes selection, semantic, and inspection
  operations:

  - Direct face/vertex/edge/group selection.
  - Scope and part-range mirrors.
  - Face materials and texture-slot assignment.
  - Durable semantic-region assignment.
  - Primitive-axis semantic bootstrap and naming.
  - Geometry audit and semantic-state JSON.
  - Declarative selectors: region, part, facing, above/below, extremal, box.
  - Retopology band planning, selection, follow-patch queries, and action drain.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:10699, it owns the complete paint/UV façade:

  - Face fill and selection fill.
  - Shader/material ink.
  - Resolution-independent stroke program.
  - Paint undo/redo and layers.
  - Fill, brush, mirrored brush, polygon/pen painting.
  - Atlas density and fit estimation.
  - UV-island inspection and selection.
  - UV rectangle/corner application.
  - Restore shape, auto-size, and project-from-view.
  - Atlas replace, import, resize, workspace compilation, palette, sampling, variants.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:11566, it returns to renderer infrastructure:

  - Dynamic geometry arena.
  - Standard and slim static-instance pools.
  - Grass, water, frond, ground, transparent, shadow, sky, skinned, and live-region
    pipelines.

  - Formula-ground buffers.
  - Live material-region bindings.
  - Render-target pool.
  - Telemetry, FPS HUD, culling, and foliage LOD.

  Starting at framework/gpu/3d.zig:12327, it owns GPU lifecycle and residency:

  - Pipeline and buffer creation/destruction.
  - Hot-reload cache reset.
  - Render-target acquisition/resizing.
  - Diffuse texture cache.
  - Paint texture upload.
  - Static, dynamic, host-loaded, and skinned geometry interning.
  - Host-generated heightfield meshes.
  - Static-instance upload/growth.
  - Runtime compilation of ground and material-region shaders.

  Finally, framework/gpu/3d.zig:14737 is a 1,300-line render graph by itself:

  - Reads camera, sky, fog, directional, ambient, point, and spot lights.
  - Calculates scene extent, clip planes, fog, and frustum.
  - Publishes the editor camera for picking.
  - Collects skinned figures.
  - Renders spotlight shadows.
  - Resolves geometry and textures.
  - Separates opaque, glass, ground, and live-region draws.
  - Batches static and dynamic instances.
  - Chooses grass/water/frond pipelines.
  - Applies chunk culling and foliage-density LOD.
  - Draws ground formulas, live material regions, then sorted transparency.

  ## Where actions are already grouped

  There is no single action taxonomy. There are several overlapping ones.

  The best native authoring vocabulary is framework/gpu/mesh_journal_log.zig:17. It
  identifies:

  - Topology: extrude face/edge, create face, loop cut, connect vertices, bevel,
    symmetrize, delete, merge, solidify, split/quadify.

  - Parts: add, delete, hide, show, duplicate, mirror, path array, detach, merge.
  - Transform: gizmo transform, nudge, scale by value.
  - Surface state: flip, glass, paint selection.
  - UV: UV edits, texture import/reload, atlas resize.
  - Retopology: guide changes.
  - Integrity: explicit ledger-alert events.

  The UV sub-vocabulary is framework/gpu/mesh_journal_log.zig:68: move, vertex edit,
  rotate, scale, flip, numeric edit, match sizes, chain, pack, stack, paste transform,
  move-to-cursor, restore shape, auto-size, project, stitch, reset.

  The model-editor UI façade is cart/editor/stage/ModelView.tsx:279. It groups selection,
  gizmos, topology, retopology, parts, paint, camera, and lighting operations for AppFrame
  and Agent Seat.

  World authoring has a separate command family beginning in cart/editor/data/
  applicationCommands.ts:97:

  - Tools: select, place, move, focus, paint faces, place sticker.
  - Placement: world.pieces.place.
  - Piece edits: move, rotate, spin, skin, delete.
  - Piece materials: assign and clear.
  - Placement-preview rotation, floor stepping, undo, and redo.

  The exact piece action IDs are centralized in cart/editor/world/pieceCommandIds.ts:4.

  Map painting is another separate family, translated in cart/editor/shell/
  AppFrame.tsx:270:

  - Terrain sculpt/paint.
  - Tile painting and material bindings.
  - Water.
  - Flora.
  - Zones.
  - Road/path creation and deletion.
  - Transport-control stops.
  - Chunk growth.

  So the present action landscape is:

  - Native model journal actions.
  - UV actions.
  - Paint stroke/layer actions.
  - Model outliner metadata actions.
  - World semantic-piece actions.
  - Map-paint actions.
  - View-only interactions such as camera, selection, and tool arming.

  ## The adjacent god files

  framework/engine.zig:1 plainly does “everything between the OS and the node tree”:

  - Feature-gated subsystem assembly.
  - Window lifecycle and custom chrome.
  - Terminal sessions and selection.
  - Scrollbars, sliders, hover, capture, text input.
  - Native map-paint and model-editor gesture loops at framework/engine.zig:842.
  - Text measurement and layout coordination.
  - Painting every primitive type, including Scene3D at framework/engine.zig:3381.
  - Canvas, graph, image, video, effect, terminal, input, world-loader, and pop-out
    painting.

  - SDL/V8/GPU startup, hot reload, event routing, frame phases, telemetry, watchdog, test
    harnesses, and shutdown in framework/engine.zig:3990.

  cart/editor/stage/ModelView.tsx:924 is the model-editor application controller:

  - Wraps roughly 136 unique host doors.
  - Loads file-backed and generated models.
  - Controls selection, gizmos, topology sessions, quality, parts, and journals.
  - Owns UV inspector data, UV texture workspaces, atlas import/export/resize, paint
    variants, and paint hydration.

  - Controls brush interaction, paint layers, camera bookmarks, reference backdrops,
    lighting, live material regions, and retopology guides.

  - Publishes ModelToolApi, focus-panel state, and Agent Seat capability.
  - Contains the hot-reload resume and large RJIT_MESHOPS verification language.
  - Renders the Scene3D plus all model-editor dialogs and overlays.

  cart/editor/shell/AppFrame.tsx:339 is the application/controller god file:

  - Adapts world, model-outliner, and Color Studio command authorities starting at cart/
    editor/shell/AppFrame.tsx:548.

  - Enforces modal discipline.
  - Owns persistence, autosave, dirty state, document identity, event-bus reporting, and
    undo routing.

  - Owns map-document switching and Map Paint.
  - Centralizes menu/hotkey command dispatch in cart/editor/shell/AppFrame.tsx:1850.
  - Owns world placement, piece edits, materials, stickers, facades, flora, selections,
    and prefabs.

  - Owns model creation, import, export, Agent Seat shell actions, model outliner, part
    reconciliation, and model document lifecycle.

  - Owns Color Studio, library navigation, file exploration, World Bible, role naming, and
    nearly every application dialog.

  - Finally composes the entire editor UI starting near cart/editor/shell/
    AppFrame.tsx:6680.

  ## Existing extracted seams

  The decomposition has already begun, but 3d.zig still owns the orchestration and shared
  mutable state:

  - framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:1: welded selection topology, visibility, mirror behavior,
    mutations, retopology planning.

  - framework/gpu/indexed_edit_mesh.zig:1: stable indexed vertices/faces and topology
    algorithms.

  - framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:1: UV layout, atlas pixels, picking, brush math.
  - framework/gpu/paint_program.zig:1: durable strokes, layers, replay, paint history.
  - framework/gpu/model_source.zig:1: authoritative source mesh, groups, parts, materials,
    semantics.

  - framework/gpu/mesh_journal_log.zig:1: action vocabulary, restore policy, diagnostics.
  - framework/v8_bindings_core.zig:151: bridge wrappers for the entire surface.

  The clean capability buckets visible today are therefore:

  - Scene rendering and GPU lifecycle.
  - Geometry/texture/instance residency.
  - Terrain and live-material rendering.
  - Resident model-document session.
  - Topology transactions.
  - Part and semantic metadata.
  - Journal and integrity.
  - Selection and transform tools.
  - Editor overlay rendering.
  - UV and atlas authoring.
  - Paint program and layers.
  - Retopology guide.
  - Native input routing.
  - JS/native bridge.
  - Model editor controller/UI.
  - World semantic authoring controller.

  No source files were changed and no game models were touched.

› Ok, how about for 3d zig file, or any of the 3d for that matter, can you find anything
  that is duplicate more than once, and can be a helper rather than a full rewrite of the
  same logic


• I’ll treat this as a read-only duplication audit: first check the governing editor/3D
  rulings, then look for repeated implementation bodies within 3d.zig and across the
  neighboring framework/gpu/*.zig files. I’ll separate true helper candidates from
  repetitions that only look similar but encode different invariants.

• The relevant rulings don’t forbid helper extraction, but they do highlight two
  boundaries that matter to this audit: native camera behavior must remain native-owned,
  and authored semantic/world data must not be collapsed into renderer geometry helpers.
  I’m using those as the filter while I inspect repeated code.

• The first pass has already found several real clones, not just similar-looking code: an
  identical screen-segment distance function in two files, a 41-line texture-resource
  construction block repeated inside 3d.zig, and two formula-pipeline builders whose
  bodies are nearly the same. I’m now checking the editor/topology side and the retained-
  instance paths so the final list can rank safe helpers separately from risky
  abstractions.

• Yes. There is substantial real duplication here—enough for a focused helper-extraction
  pass before attempting the larger file breakup.

  ## Highest-confidence helpers in 3d.zig

  1. RGBA texture binding creation

     The texture view, sampler/layout validation, bind-group creation, and failure cleanup
     are repeated almost verbatim in:
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:13482
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:13568

     A helper such as createDiffuseTextureBinding(label, width, height) could return
     { texture, view, bind_group }. Upload policy should remain outside it because one
     caller is content-cached while the other is mutated in place.

  2. Formula render-pipeline construction

     framework/gpu/3d.zig:14562 and framework/gpu/3d.zig:14658 repeat shader assembly,
     compilation progress, shader-module creation, pipeline layout, vertex layouts,
     fragment state, depth state, and pipeline creation.

     A buildFormulaPipeline(config) helper could accept:
      - shader prefix/epilogue
      - formula
      - label
      - depth comparison
      - diagnostic identity

     The .less ground depth comparison and .less_equal region comparison must remain
     explicit—they encode different rendering behavior.

  3. Region-slot lookup and data installation

     framework/gpu/3d.zig:11908 and framework/gpu/3d.zig:11961 duplicate:
      - searching for an existing (key_hash, region_id) slot
      - finding a free slot
      - copying/truncating region data
      - dirtying and activating the slot

     Clean helpers would be findOrClaimRegionSlot() and installRegionData().

  4. Node → InstanceData packing

     The same 13 node fields are passed to makeInstance six times:
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:15048
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:15155
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:15751
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:15861
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:15986
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:16048

     instanceFromNode(node, alpha_override) would eliminate this safely.

     Likewise, stride-based instance rows are decoded three times at framework/
     gpu/3d.zig:14406, framework/gpu/3d.zig:15134, and framework/gpu/3d.zig:15730. That
     wants instanceFromRow(data, stride, row).

  5. Extrusion-result metadata installation

     The final groups/materials/semantics/colors installation and rollback block is
     duplicated between the two extrusion paths:
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:1811
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:2088

     An installExtrusionResultMetadata(...) helper would centralize the important rollback
     behavior without combining either topology algorithm.

  6. Retopology plan installation

     framework/gpu/3d.zig:10545 and framework/gpu/3d.zig:10566 share the same journal/
     capture/clear/install/commit sequence.

     installRetopoBandPlan(plan, allocator) could hold the entire repeated tail.

  7. Overlay triangle decoding and projection

     Four overlay paths independently decode three positions, calculate normal/centroid,
     reject backfaces, and project the triangle:
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:9182
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:9210
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:9249
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:9271

     A projectVisibleTriangle(...) returning positions, normal, centroid, and projected
     points would remove repeated geometry bookkeeping while leaving each overlay’s
     coloring/grouping logic intact.

  8. Gizmo screen geometry

     The point-to-segment function is exactly duplicated in:
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:8342
      - framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:3791

     This belongs beside framework/math/geo.zig:13, probably as distancePointToSegmentSq.

     Mesh and backdrop gizmos also repeat arm hit-testing at framework/gpu/3d.zig:8567 and
     framework/gpu/3d.zig:8626. gizmoArmHitDistanceSq() is a straightforward extraction.

  9. Storage-buffer pool initialization

     Ground, live-region, and skin-palette pools all create arrays of storage buffers and
     one-entry bind groups:
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:12601
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:12637
      - framework/gpu/3d.zig:12689

     A parameterized initStorageBindPool() could own this WebGPU boilerplate.

  10. Retained instance-cache resolution

     framework/gpu/3d.zig:14427 and framework/gpu/3d.zig:14512 repeat most of the cache-
     hit, version update, buffer creation/growth, cache-slot selection, offset
     reservation, and return logic.

     I would extract only that retention machinery. Their row conversion and staging
     formats should remain separate.

  ## Strong adjacent-file opportunities

  - mesh_edit.zig enumerates the three distinct edges of a face four times at framework/
    gpu/mesh_edit.zig:2592, framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:2635, framework/gpu/
    mesh_edit.zig:2780, and framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:2819. This wants
    distinctFaceEdges().

  - Retopo axis and rail planners repeat band-summary allocation and bounding-box
    accumulation at framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:320 and framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:397.

  - framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:1804 and framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:1824 duplicate
    the complete Möller–Trumbore calculation. rayTri can simply call rayTriBary and
    return .t.

  - Canonical UV preparation is repeated in framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:1325 and
    framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:1381.

  - framework/gpu/world_window.zig:237 and framework/gpu/panel_window.zig:224 share large
    exact sections of surface/blit pipeline construction. A small WindowSurfaceBlitter
    owner would eliminate considerably more duplication than individual descriptor
    helpers.

  ## Things I would not blindly consolidate

  - The local vector helpers look duplicated, but normalization thresholds and zero-vector
    fallbacks differ between model painting, path planes, mesh editing, and rendering.

  - hashKey implementations use different algorithms; unifying them could invalidate cache
    identities.

  - The 43 journal snapshot sites should not be forced through one generic transaction
    wrapper. Their rollback and restoration requirements differ.

  - Render-pass descriptors often look identical while carrying meaningful depth/write/
    load differences.

  The safest first extraction wave is: segment-distance math, region slot/data helpers,
  retopo-plan installation, extrusion metadata installation, texture binding creation, and
  node/row instance packing. No source files were changed.


› ok great now last thing is what about just purely unreachable code


• I’ll do this as a stricter dead-code audit over the same 3D cluster. I’ll distinguish
  “textually unreferenced,” “not reachable from any registered host/runtime entry point,”
  and “provably impossible branch,” because only the last two are safe to call unreachable
  without qualification.

• The rulings add one important test: old JavaScript-driven camera paths are not “dormant
  compatibility”; they are explicitly retired. For everything else I’m requiring concrete
  reachability evidence from cart/editor, engine entry points, or registered V8 host doors
  before calling it dead.

• The conservative call graph is now clean enough to state numbers: out of 525 top-level
  functions in 3d.zig, 516 are reachable from engine, renderer, or registered bridge
  roots. Nine are not reachable at all. The adjacent editor/mesh modules add two more
  definition-only functions, plus one legacy face-tint subsystem that is still called but
  can no longer perform work because its backing map is never populated.

• Yes. The conservative call graph found 11 genuinely unreachable top-level functions:
  nine in 3d.zig, two in adjacent modules.

  ## Confirmed unreachable in 3d.zig

  These have no caller, no registered V8 door, no engine reference, and no test reference:

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:550 — unused programmatic orbit setter; focusAt and internal
    framing paths handle active focus changes.

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:7527 — leftover from the retired differential-normal guard
    described immediately below it.

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:7882 — unused; only the append and compaction variants
    participate in topology operations.

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:8003 — setter is live, getter has no consumer.
  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:8025 — setter is live, getter has no consumer.
  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:8032 — setter is live, getter has no consumer.
  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:10699 — reset is performed directly by internal lifecycle/
    topology paths; this public wrapper is never called.

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:10751 — setting and clearing material ink are live, but nothing
    reads this wrapper.

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:11528 — superseded by framework/gpu/3d.zig:4711, which the
    painted-mesh writer uses.

  ## Confirmed unreachable next door

  - framework/gpu/paint_program.zig:973 — the active paint path always calls
    recordDabShaped; the plain operation remains supported during replay, but this
    recording entry point is unused.

  - framework/gpu/model_source.zig:319 — every consumer directly examines partRanges()
    instead.

  ## A reachable-but-dead compatibility subsystem

  The old atlas-based face-selection tint is operationally unreachable:

  - framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:802 has no current writer.
  - framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:959 therefore always returns null.
  - framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:3814 always iterates an empty map.
  - framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig:3810 consequently does nothing.
  - suspendFaceTint/resumeFaceTint still balance a counter and are called widely, but
    eventually invoke only that no-op restoration path.

  The source explicitly calls this legacy hot-reload compatibility. Under the current
  binary’s initialization and mutation graph it cannot perform work; removing it is
  slightly more policy-sensitive than deleting the 11 orphan functions.

  Its supporting model_paint operations—framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:1549—are absent from
  the shipped runtime path. Some remain reachable only from unit tests.

  Likewise, pointFromBary, baryOfPointOnFace, and mesh_semantics.unnamedCount are test-
  only, so I would not classify them as purely unreachable.

  I found no constant-false renderer branches or dead ground/region/skinned/transparent
  pipelines. No files were changed.

    Only “change pivot while preserving zoom exactly” remains uniquely expressed by this

  ### Clearly superseded

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:7527 calculated a triangle normal/cross-product for the old
    unsafe-edit detector. That detector was explicitly retired because it falsely rejected
    valid rotations and thin geometry. The replacement is the authored-face concavity
    Auto-Fix predicate.

  - framework/gpu/3d.zig:11528 returned only the visible paint-space vertex buffer for
    saving painted.blob. It was replaced by paintedDocumentSnapshot(), which also includes
    hidden/stashed model parts. This is an abandoned narrow accessor, not abandoned
    painted-model saving.

  - framework/gpu/paint_program.zig:973 records an ordinary circular brush dab.
    recordDabShaped() replaced it and supports circles plus the other brush footprints.
    Old OP_DAB replay remains intentionally supported for existing saved paint programs;
    only the old writer is obsolete.

  - framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:2183 converted between triangle-local barycentric
    coordinates and world positions. They powered the old “stamp every triangle in an
    authored face” approach. The island-atlas implementation made that fan-out
    unnecessary; mirror painting uses the newer world-to-face lookup. These now survive
    only in a round-trip test.

    pixels, tinted selected faces orange, then restored the pixels. Screen-space overlays
    replaced that approach. The empty restoration skeleton remains intentionally capable

  So your “roughly 1,300” instinct is close for the ordinary explanatory prose, but there

  When 3d.zig becomes chapters, the governing rule should be:

  - Move local rationale together with the code it explains.
  - Promote cross-cutting rules into the relevant module/interface headers.
  - Preserve request IDs, historical failures, forbidden alternatives, and ownership
    explanations.

  - Never summarize away a comment merely because the implementation appears obvious.
  - Delete rationale only when it is demonstrably obsolete, with its replacement
    documented.

  - Give every extracted chapter a header explaining its purpose, invariants,
    dependencies, and relationship to the remaining coordinator.

  The success metric isn’t fewer comments. It is that an agent opening one extracted
  module can still understand both what it does and why competing approaches are wrong,
  without reconstructing the institutional memory from Git history.

  That means the eventual operation should be understood as editing a book into volumes—
  not dismantling it into context-free utility files.
